title: linear relation geometry
result_summary: The two F2 left relations split the 18 Hesse tables into the two nonconcurrent classes: delta 1 and delta 2.
Both F2 halves are perfectly balanced across i, j, and s and each gives double-six column total 6 across all 36 checks.
The five F3 left relations are not explained by old/new line type, H27 vertical fibres, or a single Hesse coordinate family.
The count vector respects the binary split but fails four of the five ternary relations.
conclusion: The visible binary geometry is the Hesse delta split; the ternary relations are genuine double-six/E6 constraints and expose the missing nonuniform fibre layer.
